teacher_skill.name: Specific Directions
teacher_skill.teacher_facing: Tell students exactly what they should be doing.
observable_behaviors: Tells students what to do (not what not to do)
Directions include necessary details for task success
acceptable_variations: Routine tasks may require less specificity. New or complex tasks, routines or procedures, or routines or procedures that need to be retaught may require more specificty.
For multi-step routines or procedures, specificity should apply to each step

Necessary details for task success might include components like time length, task location in room or on paper/screen, voice/volume level, task goal or criteria for success, task rationale or what to do if finished early. Specific directions only need the components from this list that are needed for student success; they do not need to include ALL components all the time.
When given as feedback during a task, directions may target only the specific portion of the task the student is struggling with rather than the full task.

teacher_skill.name: Ask, Ask, Ask
teacher_skill.teacher_facing: A verbal method of checking for understanding where the teacher asks the same or a similar question to several students to make an inference about students’ understanding.
observable_behaviors: Calls on 3+ different students, asking the same root question repeatedly

Evidence that teacher is strategically sampling rather than just calling on those who raise hands first or know answer (e.g., gives wait time to get 50% or more of hands up before calling on anyone, uses cold call instead of hands, builds on knowledge of previous writing/speaking - e.g., "Katja, you agreed that 0 is an even number, can you explain why?", etc.)
Does NOT reveal correct answer until questioning sequence is complete
acceptable_variations: May use randomization tools to select students

May ask the same root question in different ways (e.g., "Marco, what's one character trait of Amos?" then "Fatima, do you agree or disagree with Marco, why?" then "Arecely, what's one character trait **you** would choose for Amos?")
May ask follow up questions (e.g., "why?", "how do you know?", "what's an example?", etc.)

teacher_skill.name: Right Time (CFU)
teacher_skill.teacher_facing: Check for understanding at strategic moments in the lesson
observable_behaviors: CFUs after key points and key steps in content or skill instruction
CFUs when instruction can still be adjusted based on results
CFUs before releasing students to lengthy independent work
acceptable_variations: May do a formative check for understanding to assess prior knowledge before instruction on key points or steps, but must also check for updated understanding after instruction in this case

A short stop and jot or independent task can be a well-timed check for understanding and should not be penalized as an example of releasing students to independent work without a check
